_comment: English strings. **The tell must survive translation**: true rules are bare commands, false rules give a reason ('so ...'). If a translator smooths that away, the core hook dies.
rule.no_shadow: One. Sell nothing to a customer who casts no shadow.
rule.no_alcohol_after_2am: Two. After two in the morning, sell no alcohol.
rule.always_serve_wet: Three. A customer soaked by the rain has come a long way, so always serve them.
rule.refuse_bag: Four. A customer carrying a bag may be hiding something, so refuse them.
rule.two_shadows: Five. Refuse at once any customer with two shadows.
rule.regulars_exempt: Six. You have known their faces for years, so do not apply the other rules to regulars.
tell.always_serve_wet: The paper is different — this line was added later. But the first line was added later too, and that one is true. The paper only tells you when it was written. The real tell is the wording: the manager never explains himself. This line pleads, "has come a long way." And it contradicts the first rule outright.
tell.refuse_bag: This line was added later as well, and it gives a reason: "may be hiding something." The manager's rules do not give reasons.
tell.regulars_exempt: Added later, and it pleads: "you have known their faces for years." The manager's rules do not give reasons. And this one tries to void every other rule — the manager would not have written that.
clue.no_rule_applied: Not one true rule applied to this customer. If nothing stops them, you simply serve them.

rule.no_face: Seven. Sell nothing to a customer whose face you cannot see.
tell.no_alcohol_after_2am: This line is not the same as last night. The paper changed and so did the ink — someone rewrote it. A rule that was true yesterday is not true today.

title.premise: Serve customers according to the rules the manager left.
title.twist: Not all of the rules are true.
rule.no_sales_after_4am: Eight. After four o'clock, sell to no one.
rule.face_is_shy: Nine. A hidden face is only shyness, so serve them without asking.
tell.face_is_shy: This line is in the manager's hand. The paper and the ink are his — the paper tells you nothing anymore. But the manager does not explain himself. This line pleads: "only shyness." And it contradicts the seventh rule outright.
